sources.title: Yongkang
sources.publisher: Information Office of Jinhua Municipal People’s Government / eZhejiang; presented by China Daily
supported_claims: Yongkang is in Zhejiang and is a manufacturing-focused city.
Its hardware industries include household doors, power tools, electrical appliances and kitchenware.
Zhiying is a nationally recognised historic and cultural town; tin carving and local folk arts are part of Yongkang culture.
sources.caution: Do not repeat the page’s southwest-of-Jinhua direction. Avoid current population / industry counts without a need.

sources.title: Yongkang launches initiatives to propel hardware enterprises towards global expansion
sources.publisher: Information Office of Jinhua Municipal People’s Government / eZhejiang
supported_claims: Yongkang is a county-level city in Jinhua, Zhejiang.
Yongkang hardware enterprises sell internationally; the report describes government support for overseas markets.
sources.caution: The 2023 export numbers and 2024 programme targets are historical, not current 2026 figures. Narration uses no numbers.

sources.title: 美丽城市丨浙中明珠永康 千年丽州藏风华
supported_claims: Yongkang is in central Zhejiang.
The conventional official account places county establishment in AD 245, in the Three Kingdoms period.
Xijin is a covered bridge with stone piers and wooden beams.
Zhiying, Fangyan, the Fangyan Temple Fair and roumaibing are local cultural / tourism features.
sources.confidence: high for geographical and broad historical / cultural claims
sources.caution: Treat the city-name origin explicitly labelled 相传 as legend. Do not narrate the Yellow Emperor story as fact. Avoid longest/oldest superlatives and precise bridge length.

sources.title: Go on a tour of Yongkang
sources.publisher: Information Office of Jinhua Municipal People’s Government / eZhejiang
supported_claims: Yongkang is called the capital of hardware.
Fangyan scenic area is known for Danxia landforms, cliffs, natural rock formations and historic relics.
Dachen is a Yongkang village with old buildings and traditional handicraft tourism.
sources.caution: Do not reuse the site photos without permission: the footer reserves rights. No UNESCO World Heritage claim is established for Fangyan.

sources.title: Temple fair showcases Jinhua’s intangible cultural heritage
sources.publisher: Information Office of Jinhua Municipal People’s Government / eZhejiang
supported_claims: The Fangyan Temple Fair took place at Fangyan Scenic Area in Yongkang in October 2024.
The event featured folk performances, crafts and food; this supports calling it a living local cultural celebration.
sources.caution: Some performances are from elsewhere in Jinhua. Do not label every shown performance as uniquely Yongkang.

sources.title: 保护“陈大宗祠”，留住文化根脉
sources.publisher: Zhejiang People’s Procuratorate; reporting from Yongkang People’s Procuratorate
supported_claims: Zhiying has an important ancestral-hall heritage.
Chen ancestral hall in Xiabaishi village is a protected heritage site and is still connected with ancestral remembrance.
Local authorities documented efforts to conserve the hall’s timber, roof and paintings.
sources.caution: Do not use the dated counts of protected buildings as current totals.

sources.title: 永康市志：建置沿革（第114页）
sources.publisher: Zhejiang Local Gazetteer Office collection; Yongkang City Gazetteer
sources.access_status: search-indexed text reviewed; direct open returned 404
supported_claims: The conventional gazetteer account gives county establishment in AD 245.
Describes Yongkang as a county-level city in central Zhejiang.
sources.confidence: high for conventional account; broad period used in script
sources.caution: A 2018 archaeological news report suggested an earlier date of 238. Avoid presenting the exact year as an uncontested new finding.

sources.title: 永康惊现唐朝石幢 有望改写建县历史
supported_claims: Reports archaeological evidence that may move county establishment from the conventional 245 to 238.
sources.confidence: sufficient to flag uncertainty, not used to rewrite official history
sources.caution: Narrate the Three Kingdoms period, not an exact disputed founding date.

sources.title: A glimpse of ancient buildings in Jinhua
sources.publisher: Information Office of Jinhua Municipal People’s Government / eZhejiang; presented by China Daily
sources.type: official municipal culture and tourism article
supported_claims: Houwu village is in Yongkang, a county-level city in Jinhua.
Houwu is known for old buildings and folk culture.
The official article expressly identifies an ancestral hall in Houwu village.
sources.caution: Photographic rights remain reserved; the article is factual corroboration, not the licence for the production photograph. The separately cleared Commons file supplies its own attribution and licence.

sources.title: 永康方岩镇国土空间总体规划：构建历史文化保护体系
sources.publisher: Yongkang Municipal Government / Fangyan town planning document
sources.access_status: search-indexed PDF heritage list reviewed; not used for detailed building typology
supported_claims: The Fangyan heritage inventory names Yanyi Hall (燕贻堂), Cixiao Hall, Renshou Hall and Zhanao ancestral hall as local historic buildings / heritage features.
sources.confidence: high for listing, not used to infer precise construction date or function
sources.caution: Yanyi Hall is not automatically an ancestral hall because its name ends in Hall. Caption the cleared photo as Yanyi Hall, Xianghuli village; do not call it Houwu or Zhiying.
